title: Sparse-view photoacoustic reconstruction
contribution: I built a synthetic sparse-view pipeline and compared calibrated time reversal, a U-Net refinement, exact-model Tikhonov inversion and an unrolled network, then tested sound-speed mismatch and training-prior shift, and designed and ran two preregistered experiments on the failure that the shift exposed: a training intervention and a factorial diagnostic of the trained networks.
result: An unrolled network trained on four phantom families is 11 to 18 dB ahead of noise-matched Tikhonov on its sharp-edged training families, but behind it on unseen thin structures with 64 sensors. Two preregistered experiments followed: an intervention repaired one gap in the learned prior, and a factorial diagnostic found structural thinness the best-supported remaining factor, with curvature not supported as a cause and the role of edge profile unresolved. All data are synthetic.
purpose: Testing when a learned reconstruction beats model-based inversion, and why it fails under distribution shift.
status: Completed synthetic study · two preregistered experiments reported
image_alt: PSNR advantage over Tikhonov against the core width of straight lines at five fixed edge widths, for the control and intervention networks with 16 and 64 sensors at 14 dB SNR; with 64 sensors the advantage is negative for narrow soft lines and rises with width, with 16 sensors it is positive everywhere
summary: Synthetic inverse problem comparing Tikhonov inversion with learned reconstruction. A network far ahead on its training image families fell behind on unseen thin structures, and two preregistered experiments tested why.

title: Reduced models & neural operators
contribution: I compared four reduced or learned approximations with a full-order Burgers solver, including unseen initial-condition tests, and re-ran the neural surrogates on a Tesla T4 to check backend reproducibility.
result: ROM error: 0.152% in-distribution and 1.7% on the tested unseen initial-condition family, where the FNO reaches 22.6%.
purpose: Comparing fast approximations of nonlinear transport.
image_alt: Three in-distribution test cases comparing ground truth, POD-ROM, DEIM-ROM, MLP surrogate, and FNO solutions of the viscous Burgers' equation
image_caption: Research figure · open case study for context
summary: Compared classical and learned PDE surrogates: POD achieved 0.152% relative L² error versus 0.90% for FNO on 40 in-distribution cases (five FNO seeds).

title: Data assimilation for chaotic Lorenz-96
contribution: I implemented and independently checked an ensemble Kalman filter, then studied localisation, ensemble size, and filter failure.
result: Localisation reduces RMSE from 4.63 (a diverged unlocalised filter) to 0.41, below the observation noise (10 seeds).
purpose: Estimating chaotic system states from noisy observations.
image_alt: Assimilation RMSE versus Gaspari-Cohn localisation radius, showing over an eleven-fold reduction relative to the unlocalized baseline at the best tested radius
image_caption: Research figure · open case study for context
summary: In a 10-seed study with a selected localisation radius, reduced state-estimation RMSE from 4.63 to 0.41 using Ensemble Kalman filtering.

title: Optimal mixing of passive scalars
contribution: My 2021 M.Sc. thesis studied bounds on passive-scalar mixing (University of L’Aquila; supervisor: Prof. Stefano Spirito). The subsequent Python implementation, numerical report and resolution study extend that work.
result: Extended to N=512: the apparent resolution dependence of the fitted mixing exponent is primarily a moving-fit-window effect; on fixed time windows it converges at about second order.
purpose: Reproducible pseudo-spectral study of optimal passive-scalar mixing.
image_alt: Plot of log H-1 mix norm decaying linearly over time, alongside conserved L2, L4 and L8 norms
image_caption: Research figure · open case study for context
summary: Extended M.Sc. thesis computations to N=512 with 48 verification tests; established approximately second-order convergence of fixed-window exponent fits.

title: Finite-element cylinder-flow benchmarks
contribution: I implemented a Taylor–Hood solver and evaluated geometry, mesh, time-step, and force-definition effects against cylinder-flow benchmarks.
result: Verified O(h³)/O(h²) velocity convergence; complete unsteady benchmark reproduction is not claimed.
purpose: Measuring solver accuracy on standard cylinder-flow problems.
image_alt: Velocity magnitude with streamlines, pressure field, and vorticity field around the cylinder at the finest 2D-1 steady mesh
image_caption: Research figure · open case study for context
summary: Taylor–Hood finite-element solver verified at O(h³)/O(h²) velocity convergence, with steady cylinder-flow results closely matching the published reference.
